The patch was submitted. I'll summarize the fix.
The issue was that `TableDataElement.on_text` was calling `stylize` on `Text` objects that might already have styles (e.g., syntax-highlighted inline code), which could lead to redundant or incorrect styling. By only calling `stylize` when the input is a string, we preserve the styles already present in `Text` objects.

The issue was that `TableDataElement.on_text` in `rich/markdown.py` was calling `stylize` on all incoming text, including `Text` objects that had already been styled (e.g., syntax-highlighted inline code created via `Text.assemble` in `MarkdownContext.on_text`). This could result in redundant styling or overwrite intended styles.

The fix modifies `TableDataElement.on_text` to only apply `stylize` when the input is a string. If the input is already a `Text` object, it is appended directly, preserving its existing styles.

```python
    def on_text(self, context: MarkdownContext, text: TextType) -> None:
        if isinstance(text, str):
            text = Text(text)
            text.stylize(context.current_style)
        self.content.append_text(text)
```
